findings.description: The requirement detects a late start at expiry if the task has not started, while SYS-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-127 treat a start delay equal to the limit as within the limit.
findings.requested_change: Align the detection condition and timing with the permitted equality and measurement resolution in CON-SUP-127.

findings.description: The requirement detects an overrun at expiry while the task is still executing, whereas SYS-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-127 treat an execution time equal to the limit as within the limit.
findings.requested_change: Align the overrun condition and detection timing with the permitted equality and measurement resolution in CON-SUP-127.

findings.description: CON-SUP-129 specifies that the CRC is computed over bytes in increasing address order; the requirement does not constrain the processing order.
findings.requested_change: Specify the source-required byte processing order for the program-code CRC.

findings.description: CON-SUP-129 specifies increasing address order and a 32-bit little-endian stored reference for each CRC. Neither is stated for the configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required byte processing order and stored-reference representation for the configuration CRC.

findings.description: The requirement applies safe-state entry to every detected fault, but CON-SUP-130 and SYS-SAFE-011 say a watchdog reset reported at start-up counts as a code 8 detection without by itself entering the safe state.
findings.requested_change: State the source-defined exception for the start-up watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: Stopping both watchdogs without exception on every fault detection includes a code 8 detection at start-up, while CON-SUP-130 requires start-up to continue without entering the safe state by that report alone. Repeated watchdog resets can prevent that continuation.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the watchdog-servicing behavior for a start-up code 8 detection against CON-SUP-121 and CON-SUP-130, and state the resulting rule.

findings.description: The reset obligation applies to a first or second detection of any fault code. CON-SUP-115 and SYS-SAFE-010 instead require a configuration fault at start-up to latch the safe state until power-on reset.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify how the reset rule applies to a configuration fault that immediately latches the safe state.

findings.description: The unconditional 10 ms report-completion obligation conflicts with CON-SUP-121, which permits a watchdog reset before completion and requires no report for the fault being handled.
findings.requested_change: Include the watchdog-reset exception specified by CON-SUP-121.

findings.description: The requirement reports SAFE from every fault detection until reset. CON-SUP-130 excludes a start-up code 8 report from entering the safe state by itself and requires start-up to continue.
findings.requested_change: State the code 8 start-up exception in the reported-state rules.

findings.description: The 50 ms response deadline starts when GET STATUS is received, but OP-SYS-002 records that request framing and the point at which a request counts as received are undefined. The deadline cannot be measured consistently without that decision.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SYS-002 as blocking

findings.description: The item equates a start delay longer than the limit with the task not having started when the limit expires, while also saying a start exactly at the limit is within the limit. At the boundary, those descriptions do not identify the same condition; CON-SUP-127 permits equality.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the boundary condition and detection rule so a start exactly at the limit is accepted and a later start is detected within the permitted resolution.

findings.description: The item equates an execution time longer than the limit with the task still executing when the limit expires, while also saying an execution time exactly equal to the limit is within the limit. At the boundary, those descriptions do not identify the same condition; CON-SUP-127 permits equality.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the boundary condition and detection rule so completion exactly at the limit is accepted and an overrun is detected within the permitted resolution.

findings.description: The reset rule includes the first and second detections of fault code 8 and waits for safe-state entry. CON-SUP-130 and SYS-SAFE-011 say a code 8 report at start-up alone does not enter the safe state and start-up continues, leaving the reset trigger in this item unresolved for those detections.
findings.requested_change: Resolve how the reset rule applies to the first and second code 8 reports at start-up, consistent with the specified continuation of start-up; record a blocking decision if the inputs do not determine the behavior.

findings.description: The item excludes a code 8 report at start-up from stopping watchdog servicing. CON-SUP-130 says the report counts as a detection for the latch rule, while CON-SUP-121 says servicing stops at fault detection without exception. The cited inputs do not explicitly resolve whether that detection is exempt.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and record a decision resolving watchdog servicing on a code 8 report at start-up, then align the requirement and its rationale with that decision.

findings.description: The requirement exempts a start-up code 8 report from stopping watchdog service. CON-SUP-121 says servicing stops at fault detection without exception, while CON-SUP-130 counts that report as a detection for the latch rule and says start-up continues. OP-SYS-003 records that the inputs do not resolve whether servicing continues in this case.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision on watchdog servicing for a start-up code 8 report and align the requirement and its sources with that decision.

findings.description: The 50 ms response deadline starts when GET STATUS is received, but OP-SYS-002 records that request framing and the point at which a request counts as received are undefined. The deadline cannot be measured consistently without that decision.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-002 as blocking and obtain a decision defining when a request is received.

findings.description: The requirement exempts a start-up code 8 report from stopping watchdog service. CON-SUP-121 says servicing stops at fault detection without exception, while CON-SUP-130 counts that report as a detection for the latch rule and says start-up continues. OP-SYS-003 records that the inputs do not resolve whether servicing continues in this case.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision on watchdog servicing for a start-up code 8 report and align the requirement with it.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-003 requires window-watchdog refresh while every supervised task is healthy, while SYS-WDG-005 requires servicing to stop after a fault. A code-integrity fault can occur while all supervised tasks are healthy, making both obligations apply at once.
findings.requested_change: Align the window-watchdog refresh condition with the fault-detection stop rule.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-011 requires start-up to continue without entering the safe state when code 8 is reported, without an exception for the third detection. SYS-SAFE-007 requires that third detection to latch the safe state, and CON-SUP-130 says LATCHED overrides the other states.
findings.requested_change: Make the start-up continuation rule consistent with the third-detection latch and its state priority.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires GET FAULTS to return the last eight fault reports. SYS-DIAG-009 specifies the order and maximum number of reports held, but the set does not require the history to retain the most recent eight reports.
findings.requested_change: Specify retention and replacement of fault history so GET FAULTS returns the most recent eight reports, or all reports when fewer than eight exist.

findings.description: The 50 ms response deadline starts when GET STATUS is received, but OP-SYS-002 records that request framing and the point at which a request counts as received are undefined. The deadline cannot be measured consistently without that decision.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-002 as blocking.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-005 exempts a start-up code 8 report from stopping watchdog service. CON-SUP-121 says servicing stops at fault detection without exception, while CON-SUP-130 counts that report as a detection for the latch rule and says start-up continues. OP-SYS-003 records that the inputs do not resolve whether servicing continues in this case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-003 and align watchdog servicing with the resulting product decision.

findings.description: The requirement combines counting a code 8 report toward the latch rule with continuing start-up without entering the safe state. Either behavior could pass while the other fails.
findings.requested_change: Separate the latch-counting obligation from the start-up continuation obligation so each can be judged independently.

findings.description: The unconditional 50 ms response limit is infeasible for sufficiently frequent GET FAULTS requests. With eight retained reports, each response is much longer than its request; repeated requests can arrive faster than the 115200-baud line can transmit the answers. CON-SUP-138 specifies no request-spacing or concurrency limit.
findings.requested_change: Obtain an agreed service-request rate or concurrency rule, or another source-supported response policy, and state the resulting testable conditions.

findings.description: The answer requires <cause> to be one of five values but does not require it to represent the classified reset cause. Returning POR for every request would satisfy the stated value constraint while failing CON-SUP-118 and CON-SUP-111.
findings.requested_change: Require the returned value to correspond to the classified reset cause, with the mapping between reset classes and response values specified or referenced.

findings.description: The requirement limits the GET FAULTS response to requests received when no earlier request is unanswered and no transmission is in progress. CON-SUP-113 and CON-SUP-138 specify a response within 50 ms without those conditions. OP-SYS-002 records the missing concurrency decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the request concurrency and timing rules with the product owner, then align the requirement and its sources with that decision.

findings.description: The unconditional 50 ms response to GET RESET can conflict with an ongoing GET FAULTS response or other diagnostic transmission on the same 115200-baud line. CON-SUP-118 and CON-SUP-138 give no concurrency or request-spacing rule; OP-SYS-002 records the decision needed to establish feasible behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted request concurrency and response timing with the product owner, then specify a feasible GET RESET obligation consistent with that decision.

findings.description: The requirement limits the GET FAULTS response to requests received when no earlier request is unanswered and no transmission is in progress. CON-SUP-113 and CON-SUP-138 specify a response within 50 ms without those conditions. OP-SYS-002 records the missing concurrency decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted request rate and concurrency behavior, then specify GET FAULTS responses consistently with that decision and the applicable response deadline.

findings.description: The unconditional 50 ms response to GET RESET can conflict with an ongoing GET FAULTS response or another diagnostic transmission on the same 115200-baud line. CON-SUP-118 and CON-SUP-138 give no concurrency or request-spacing rule; OP-SYS-002 records the decision needed to establish feasible behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve request spacing and diagnostic transmission concurrency, then specify a feasible GET RESET response deadline and behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires consecutive occurrences of the same fault code for the repeated-fault latch. SYS-SAFE-007 specifies the third detection of the same code without 60 seconds of fault-free operation but does not address an intervening different fault code. The set therefore does not establish how the consecutive-fault condition is maintained.
findings.requested_change: Specify how intervening different fault codes affect the repeated-fault history and latch decision, consistent with the source decisions.

findings.description: CON-SUP-132 specifies that external board pull-down resistors hold the control outputs and status signal low before software configures the pins, and that the pins are inputs during that interval. SYS-SAFE-003 requires low signals and SYS-SAFE-004 requires subsequent configuration, but the set does not capture those platform obligations.
findings.requested_change: Capture the specified reset-time pin state and external pull-down provision as applicable system or platform obligations.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-009 limits the GET FAULTS response to requests received when no earlier request is unanswered and no transmission is in progress. CON-SUP-113 and CON-SUP-138 specify a response within 50 ms without those conditions. OP-SYS-002 records the missing concurrency decision.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a decision on request concurrency and response behavior, then align the requirement with that decision.

findings.description: The unconditional 50 ms response to GET RESET can conflict with an ongoing GET FAULTS response or another diagnostic transmission on the same 115200-baud line. CON-SUP-118 and CON-SUP-138 give no concurrency or request-spacing rule; OP-SYS-002 records the decision needed to establish feasible behavior.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a decision on diagnostic transmission concurrency and update the response obligations accordingly.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires consecutive occurrences of the same fault code for the repeated-fault latch. SYS-SAFE-007 specifies the third detection of the same code without 60 seconds of fault-free operation but does not address an intervening different fault code. OP-SYS-003 records the unresolved behavior.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a decision on the effect of an intervening different fault code and specify the latch and reset behavior consistently.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-002 requires a report whenever a fault is detected, while SYS-DIAG-003 and CON-SUP-121 permit the original report to be omitted when a watchdog reset interrupts its transmission. The obligations conflict for that case.
findings.requested_change: Align the fault-report obligation with the watchdog-reset exception in CON-SUP-121.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-009 limits the GET FAULTS response to requests received when no earlier request is unanswered and no transmission is in progress. CON-SUP-113 and CON-SUP-138 specify a response within 50 ms without those conditions. OP-SYS-002 records the missing concurrency decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the request concurrency and response obligations with the product owner, then align the requirement with that decision.

findings.description: The unconditional 50 ms response to GET RESET can conflict with an ongoing GET FAULTS response or another diagnostic transmission on the same 115200-baud line. CON-SUP-118 and CON-SUP-138 give no concurrency or request-spacing rule; OP-SYS-002 records the decision needed to establish feasible behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the request concurrency and response obligations with the product owner, then state a feasible response deadline under those conditions.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires consecutive occurrences of the same fault code for the repeated-fault latch. SYS-SAFE-007 specifies the third detection of the same code without 60 seconds of fault-free operation but does not address an intervening different fault code. OP-SYS-003 records the unresolved behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the effect of an intervening different fault code with the product owner and specify the resulting latch behavior.

findings.description: The requirement says a count returns to zero "only after" 60 s of fault-free operation, but does not require it to return to zero when that time is reached. A count that never clears would satisfy the wording, contrary to CON-SUP-140.
findings.requested_change: Require the per-code counts to return to zero upon reaching 60 s of fault-free operation, using the counting bounds in SYS-SAFE-008.

findings.description: The requirement mandates an answer whenever GET STATUS is received, including during an earlier answer, whereas SYS-DIAG-015 and CON-SUP-139 require a request received during an answer to be discarded without an answer.
findings.requested_change: Exclude requests received while an earlier answer is being transmitted from the answer obligation.

findings.description: The requirement mandates an answer whenever GET FAULTS is received, including during an earlier answer, whereas SYS-DIAG-015 and CON-SUP-139 require a request received during an answer to be discarded without an answer.
findings.requested_change: Exclude requests received while an earlier answer is being transmitted from the answer obligation.

findings.description: The requirement mandates an answer whenever GET RESET is received, including during an earlier answer, whereas SYS-DIAG-015 and CON-SUP-139 require a request received during an answer to be discarded without an answer.
findings.requested_change: Exclude requests received while an earlier answer is being transmitted from the answer obligation.

findings.description: The requirement mandates an ERR answer whenever any other service request is received, including during an earlier answer, whereas SYS-DIAG-015 and CON-SUP-139 require a request received during an answer to be discarded without an answer.
findings.requested_change: Exclude requests received while an earlier answer is being transmitted from the answer obligation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-117 and CON-SUP-140 require detections of each code to accumulate across the supervisor resets following the first and second detections. SYS-SAFE-017 requires separate counts, but SYS-SAFE-009 preserves only the latch, fault history and diagnostic fault count; it does not preserve the per-code counts.
findings.requested_change: Require the per-code detection counts to survive software and watchdog resets and specify their clearing at power loss.

findings.description: CON-SUP-117 and CON-SUP-140 clear counts after 60 s of fault-free operation. SYS-SAFE-008 counts only OPERATIONAL time, but the set does not require the accumulated fault-free interval to restart when a fault interrupts it. Separate fault-free intervals could therefore be added to clear counts prematurely.
findings.requested_change: Specify how a fault interrupts and restarts the 60 s fault-free interval while preserving the permitted under-count of CON-SUP-136.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-014 requires an ERR answer for a line longer than 32 characters without excluding lines received while an earlier answer is transmitting. SYS-DIAG-015 requires a service request received during that interval to be discarded without an answer, as does CON-SUP-139. The set does not consistently specify the response to an overlong request received during an answer.
findings.requested_change: Clarify that an overlong request received while an earlier answer is transmitting is discarded without an answer, consistent with CON-SUP-139.

findings.description: The requirement combines retention of the latch, fault history, fault count and per-code detection counts across resets. Retention of any one can pass while another fails.
findings.requested_change: Split the independently verifiable retention obligations so each can be judged separately.

findings.description: The requirement combines loss of the latch, fault history and counts at power loss with initialization of each count after power-on reset. These behaviors can pass or fail independently.
findings.requested_change: Split the independently verifiable power-loss and count-initialization obligations.

findings.description: The requirement combines loss of the latch, fault history, fault count and per-code detection counts at power loss. Each can pass or fail independently; CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-125 identify distinct retained information.
findings.requested_change: Split the power-loss obligations so each independently verifiable item of retained information is addressed separately.

findings.description: The requirement combines initialization of the fault report count from SYS-DIAG-008 and the separate per-code detection counts from SYS-SAFE-017. One count can be initialized correctly while the other is not.
findings.requested_change: Separate initialization of the fault report count from initialization of the per-code detection counts.

findings.description: “After a loss of power” has no endpoint, so the prohibition on holding the latch can be read as continuing after subsequent faults. CON-SUP-117 requires a new latch on the third detection.
findings.requested_change: Define the power-on initialization point and make clear that the prior latch is cleared without preventing a later latch.

findings.description: “After a loss of power” has no endpoint, so the prohibition on holding fault history can be read as preventing storage of new reports after power returns. CON-SUP-110 concerns history surviving power loss, not new history.
findings.requested_change: Specify that the pre-loss history is cleared at power-on and identify when initialization is complete.

findings.description: The prohibition on holding the fault count “after a loss of power” has no endpoint. CON-SUP-125 requires the count of reports since the last power-on reset, including new reports.
findings.requested_change: Specify that the pre-loss count is cleared at power-on without preventing subsequent reports from being counted.

findings.description: The prohibition on holding per-code counts “after a loss of power” has no endpoint. CON-SUP-140 requires new detections to be counted for the latch rule.
findings.requested_change: Specify that the pre-loss counts are cleared at power-on without preventing subsequent detections from being counted.

findings.description: Setting the report count to zero “after a power-on reset” does not establish whether initialization precedes a start-up fault report. A later zeroing could erase a report that CON-SUP-125 requires the count to include.
findings.requested_change: Specify initialization before any post-reset fault report can be counted.

findings.description: Setting per-code counts to zero “after a power-on reset” does not establish whether initialization precedes a start-up fault detection. A later zeroing could erase a detection needed by the CON-SUP-140 latch rule.
findings.requested_change: Specify initialization before any post-reset fault detection can be counted.

findings.description: The statement says each per-code count includes every detection after the power-on reset. SYS-SAFE-017 assigns detections to separate fault-code counts, and SYS-SAFE-018 returns each count to zero after 60 s of fault-free operation, as required by CON-SUP-140.
findings.requested_change: Limit the initialization outcome to preserving subsequent detections in their corresponding per-code counts, subject to the reset rule in SYS-SAFE-018.

findings.description: CON-SUP-137 requires watchdog servicing during start-up to continue as for any start-up. SYS-WDG-008 refers to that behavior, but SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-004 specify servicing only while every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected. The set does not define servicing before the start-up checks pass and task supervision begins.
findings.requested_change: Specify when and how both watchdogs are serviced during start-up, including the timing needed to avoid an unintended reset, or record any required product decision as an open point.

findings.description: CON-SUP-133 allocates at most 1 ms to the board output stage from the pin change to the output level. SYS-SAFE-002 captures the 49 ms pin-change bound and SYS-SAFE-001 captures the 50 ms overall bound, but the set does not capture the allocated board output-stage limit.
findings.requested_change: Add a traceable system-level obligation for the board output-stage response limit in CON-SUP-133.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 limits the application image to at most 1 MiB, and CON-SUP-124 places the stored program CRC reference outside the checked range. SYS-MEM-001 identifies the symbols and reference but does not capture either constraint; SYS-MEM-006 specifies a pass time for a 1 MiB image without limiting the image size.
findings.requested_change: Capture the maximum application image size and the requirement that the stored program CRC reference lie outside the checked range.

findings.description: CON-SUP-137 says a code 8 start-up report is not a fault detection for watchdog servicing. SYS-RST-003 requires that report, but SYS-DIAG-002 and SYS-DIAG-003 apply their format and transmission deadline when a fault is detected. The set does not clearly apply those report obligations to the code 8 start-up report.
findings.requested_change: Specify the applicable fault-report format and transmission timing for a code 8 report at start-up, consistently with CON-SUP-112 and CON-SUP-137.

findings.description: SYS-SAFE-007 requires the safe state to remain latched until a power-on reset, and SYS-SAFE-009 retains the latch across software and watchdog resets. After such a reset, SYS-SAFE-005 requires the status signal to be driven high when start-up checks pass and no fault has been detected, even if the latch remains set. The latched safe state requires that signal to be low under SYS-SAFE-001.
findings.requested_change: Make the operational status output requirement consistent with the retained safe-state latch, including after software and watchdog resets.
